transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Speaking to reporters before leaving for last night's campaign rally in South Carolina,
President Trump said Russian leader Vladimir Putin would not have released American Stephen Hubbard
if he had not eased sanctions on Russia.
I had a very good and very fast negotiation with President Putin.
If you were to put those sanctions on, or whatever you want to call them,
you could forget about him, you'd never see him again.
He'd be back in jail for 25 years.
Hubbard spent more than four years in a Russian prison.
He's a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan.
Russia accused him of fighting with the Ukrainian military.
In recent weeks, Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel fuel
and declined to enact a Russia sanctions package passed by Congress.
Also, Russia has agreed to resume three-way talks on the Ukraine war with the U.S. and Kyiv.
The Kremlin says Putin has agreed to, in principle, to restart talks after November 10th.
President Trump due in Iowa this evening for another rally, this one in Sioux City,
the latest stop in his effort to drum up support for Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections.
With less than two weeks to go until the midterms, Ohio's Republican candidate for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy,
is behind an attack ad that features the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton.
From Member Station WOSU, George Shilcock reports.
In the ad, Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, claims Acton lied about growing up homeless and living in a tent.
Court records prove Acton wasn't lying.
Acton says she hasn't spoken to her mother in 50 years.
Arthur's custody was revoked after Acton's now deceased stepfather was accused of raping her.
Arthur sided with her husband over her daughter in the case.
It's awful to see her this way, and it's even more incredible to see that my opponent has taken advantage of someone who is clearly not well.
Ramaswamy tells the Associated Press and other reporters his campaign created the ad, and he defends it.
Since Tuesday, there's been national bipartisan backlash to the ad.
For NPR News, I'm George Shilcock.
The social media company, Meta, says more than 10 million people have already signed up for its personal AI agent, Muse, which launched last month.
This says the company commits to spending more on artificial intelligence.
Here's it appears John Bruich reporting.
Meta reported strong earnings in its latest quarter, with revenue up around 26 percent
and profits leaping to nearly $10 billion from less than $3 billion a year ago.
But its spending is also on the rise.
The company said capital expenditures during the quarter totaled almost $35 billion,
and it raised the floor for its full-year CAPEX spending plan to $135 billion from $130 billion.
Much of that money is going into AI development, and that fast-growing AI agent, Muse, which has been a hit in app stores, is part of it.
John Bruich, NPR News.
This is NPR.
To New Mexico now, where a state judge has ordered tech giant Meta to pay the state $25 billion for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook.
A New Mexico jury last month found Meta responsible for millions of violations of state consumer protection laws stemming from the Cambridge Analytica data harvesting scandal.
The fine imposed Wednesday, the biggest ever against Meta, which says it will appeal.
A new report by the Center on Reinventing Public Education finds nearly 9 out of 10 U.S. school districts have not recovered from the pandemic and have declining student math and reading scores, and PRS Chinaki Meta reports.
Even though student achievement in math and reading have been suffering since 2013, things have only gotten worse since the pandemic.
The new report found that only 13 states have a clear, specific statewide goal for student learning, like South Carolina,
which aims for 75 percent of its students to be performing at grade level by 2030.
43 states have passed legislation on quality reading instruction, but only 18 states have done so for math.
The most aggressive policies are in Republican-led states, but overall far fewer states have schools that are actually putting what's in the law into practice in the classroom.
Chinaki Meta, NPR News.
Pope Leo's doctors say he will not need any further therapy after undergoing lung cancer surgery last week.
The Vatican announcement Wednesday confirms that Leo's lung cancer had not spread.
Leo returned to the Vatican on Saturday after having the lower lobe of his right lung removed.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
[music]

Trump heads to Sioux City, Iowa rally to support Republican midterm candidates
Ohio's Vivek Ramaswamy backs attack ad using estranged mother of Democrat Amy Acton
Meta reports strong quarterly earnings while raising 2026 AI spending plan to $135 billion
New Mexico judge orders Meta to pay $25 billion over Facebook privacy deception
Report finds nearly nine in ten US school districts still struggling with student achievement post-pandemic
Pope Leo's doctors say no further therapy needed after lung cancer surgery
